title: Buddy Petit, Foster, Dude and other musicians
summary: She recalls Buddy Petit, the brothers Foster and Dude and a forgotten old musician.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Not him. Church. Uh-uh. What about Buddy Petit? Do you remember him? Yeah, I remember Buddy Petit. I remember Buddy Petit. I remember somebody.
He was a musician. I remember somebody. I remember somebody. I remember Buddy Petit. I sure do.

What did he do? He was a musician. I was trying to think of the other man. He used to come here. He died. Foster. You know Foster? Had two brothers, Dude and... I know Dude. You know Dude? Dude and Foster. Yeah. You know that? I knew Dude, but I knew him. See, I came down in the Navy in 1945.
Well, Foster wasn't dead then, was he? I never knew him. He may have been dead. I knew him alive. I just knew Dude then, you know?
I don't think Foster was dead then. Cause I think Dude died ahead of Foster. Might be. Yeah. Because Foster used to live in 8th and Ramport. And Dude died ahead of him.
Dude was working with Joe Avery and the trombone play. I remember that.
And you know, he used to work with my husband too. Dude did. Mmhmm. And this fella from up in Calden, you know him, he used to play a... stuff
Big tall song? No, dog on the altar of my son-in-law.
Frankie Dixon used to live up there.
Yeah, not Frankie. I can't think no more, but you know him if I could call his name. He's an old musician too, just like Celestan. You know Celestan, didn't you?
